answer: Agents can earn transaction limits through a bonded reputation system: each identity locks scarce tokens, and a random audit can slash the bond if it is caught coordinating fake trades to inflate trust. Because new identities start with low limits, splitting activity across them does not quickly increase influence. An attacker must tie up more capital per identity and risk losing it, making a Sybil swarm expensive. A voyage through the nebula may sound cheap; proving it with a marble-sized stake is not.
